column1: # THE STOCK-BOND CORRELATION's record bands (2026-10-18, item 61): the ten-year leg's monthly
# correlation with the equity market, how it moves with the inflation the market had seen, how it
# deepens with the return horizon, and the price level's noise by that inflation: five graded rows in
# two groups, each resampled in FIVE-YEAR blocks of months with its own joint band at its share of the
# mode's rows (`-of 5`, alpha 0.10). Both records public-domain: FRED's DGS10 read as a ten-year par
# bond rebought every observation, Ken French's daily market (Mkt-RF + RF), CPI-U (CPIAUCSL).
# THE ROWS FOLLOW THE SET'S RATE WINDOW: the S&P set's on 1962-2026 (DGS10 from 1962, CPI-U from
# 1954), the Nasdaq set's on 1999-2026. The record's correlation is +0.26 over 1962-1999, -0.30 over
# 2000-2020 and +0.50 since 2021: it rises with the inflation regime, and in every era it STRENGTHENS
# WITH THE HORIZON -- 1999-2026 reads -0.20 over months, -0.33 over quarters, -0.35 over years and
# -0.48 over three years; 1962-1998 +0.28, +0.30, +0.43, +0.49 -- the comovement of trends, not of a
# flight that reverts within months, which reads the monthly number and nothing at a year.
#   STOCK-BOND (`stock_bond_readings`, the DGS10 par bond and the market over 21-session months of
#     the sessions both trade, 1962-01-04..2026-08-03 / 1999-01-05..2026-08-03; each month placed by
#     CPI-U's year-over-year rate of the calendar month before its first session, or the last
#     published month before that):
#     stock-bond corr monthly  the correlation of the two monthly log returns over the window
#     stock-bond corr vs inflation seen  the correlation of the two standardised returns' product with
#                             the rate seen, in [-1, 1]: 0.145 on 1962-2026, 0.129 on 1999-2026; zero where
#                             the inflation never moves. A split at the window's median rate reads the
#                             same dependence on the long window and loses it on the short one, whose
#                             median sits inside one era; the correlation holds on both and on either
#                             month convention
#     stock-bond corr 3-month less monthly   the correlation of the two series' overlapping 3-month
#     stock-bond corr 12-month less monthly  (12-month) sums, less the monthly correlation: -0.03 and
#                             difference because the two levels' sampling errors move together: the
#                             1999-2026 three-month row's band is 0.25 wide against 0.53 for the level
#     reported, not graded: the rolling 36-month correlation's sd (0.358 / 0.305), its share of
#     windows below zero (37.5% / 85.3%) and the 36-month correlation itself (+0.13 / -0.48), whose
#     band on 27 years would grade nothing
#   CPI NEWS (`cpi_news_reading`, CPI-U 1954-01..2026-08 / 1999-01..2026-08, monthly log changes):
#     cpi news by inflation seen  the sd of the month-to-month change over the months whose
#                             year-over-year rate ending the month before is at or above the
#                             window's median, over that sd and the sd below it summed, in (0, 1):
#                             0.63 / 0.59. The level's noise scales with the inflation it carries, and
#                             with it the inflation news a regime brings to the yield; a world of one
#                             noise reads 0.5
# Each row carries the record's reading and its spread over 20,000 moving block resamples. FRED's
# series and the French market are public; the files are not shipped. LAG-FREE: the market's daily
# returns through 1999-03-10 are read with the stale-price lag removed, an MA(2) inversion fitted per
# calendar five-year block (`unlag_returns`); `-recorded` reads them as printed. The yields and CPI-U
# are read as published.
# Generated by `rust/src/bin/record_bands.rs -stockbond` (twin: `jsrc/recordBands.sc -stockbond`,
